title: China's WoW Put Flesh Back on the Skeletons and Charged by the Hour
hook: In 2007 the Chinese version of WoW covered the Forsaken in flesh and swapped bone piles for graves to pass content review. Players there also paid about 6 cents an hour instead of a subscription. Would you have kept playing a WoW with no skeletons?
script: Did you know World of Warcraft in China once had to put flesh back on its skeletons? When WoW launched in China in June of two thousand five, Blizzard did not run it. A local company called The9 did, and players paid by the hour instead of a monthly fee. A thirty yuan card worked out to around six cents an hour. The rest of the world had already been playing The Burning Crusade since January of two thousand seven. China waited until September. To pass the country's content review, The9 changed the game itself. The Forsaken, who normally have bones poking through their skin, were covered in flesh. The piles of bones that marked dead characters were swapped for grave mounds. By the end of the decade, Chinese media reported that the game had somewhere between four and five million players in the country. That was close to half of the eleven and a half million subscribers WoW had around the world at the time. Then in January of two thousand twenty three, the whole game went dark in China when Blizzard's deal with its local partner NetEase collapsed. The game finally came back online in China in August of two thousand twenty four, after more than a year and a half away. Would you have kept playing with fleshy Forsaken? Follow for more gaming history.
